newsitem.title: CANADA: TENNIS-SELES TO FACE HUBER IN CANADIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SELES TO FACE HUBER IN CANADIAN OPEN.

text.p: Top-seeded Monica Seles reached her third consecutive Canadian Open final Saturday, defeating seventh-seeded Conchita Martinez 6-2 7-6 (8-6) to earn a meeting with eighth seed Anke Huber.

The third-ranked Seles, who won this event in Toronto on her return to tennis in 1995 and in Montreal a year ago, seemed to be tiring in the late going and had to save a set point down 5-6 in the second-set tiebreaker.
Huber advanced to the final when, with the set count even at 3-6 6-2, 10th-seeded Mary Joe Fernandez had to retire due to tendinitis in her right wrist.

Seles lost to Martinez 7-6 (7-5) 6-4 in their last meeting in Palo Alto, California, three weeks ago, but the former world number one took their 11 previous matches all in straight sets. Until Martinez rallied from love-40 on her serve at 2-4 in the second set, Saturday's match appeared to be going the way of those 11 previous ones.
From that point on the 8,500 spectators were treated to a riveting battle.
Seles, who had been electrifying in her aggressive baseline play, began to look a little weary and Martinez came to life with occasional forceful shotmaking of her own.
Seles led 5-4 and then Martinez 6-5 before they went to the tiebreak. In the breaker, Seles fell behind 2-4 on a double fault but then leveled at 4-all when Martinez double faulted.
At 6-5, set point for Martinez, the players had a short rally before Seles blasted a backhand down the line that the Spaniard could barely get her racket on.

That was the only time in their 13 meetings that a match had come close to going three sets. A Martinez forehand in the net and then a brilliant backhand passing shot winner off a deep approach shot and Seles had her 12th win in 14 matches since Wimbledon.
"She started to play better and hit a lot of balls that landed on the line," Seles said about the way Martinez rallied in the second set.
Asked about the backhand blast on set point for Martinez, Seles answered: "I knew I had to go for the shot, so I just closed my eyes and hit it."
Seles was a little unhappy with her serving, but she played very consistently. Despite being the more aggressive player, she had only 24 unforced errors to 37 for Martinez.
"I started slowly but I played great tennis in the second set," the ninth-ranked Martinez said. "I was moving well and I had my chances. If there had been a third set, you never know."
Fernandez outplayed an edgy Huber in the first set but then the 22-year-old German's powerful ground strokes began to take their toll in the second set.

"It got a little aggravated yesterday (in a win over unseeded Magdalena Maleeva of Bulgaria on Friday)," the 25-year-old American said about her wrist. "I think the windy conditions today made it difficult for me to compensate."
"It's frustrating because the wrist injuries I've had for a year just don't seem to go away."

The eighth-ranked Huber is 0-7 in career matches with Seles, her occasional doubles partner, and she has yet to win a set. "You have to play very aggressively and try to move her if you can," Huber said about Seles. "But it's very difficult because she plays everything so hard and deep."
